text: Lesson 2's scoped checklist now gets applied for real, to HRU-FILE01 and HRU-APP01. Every step gets a command to prove it actually landed -- I configured it isn't the same as I confirmed it, and only the second one survives a follow-up question from Dale.

First, account lockout policy. Windows Server's default is more permissive than Hartwell wants on machines holding production billing data. Mara sets a lockout threshold of five failed attempts with a thirty-minute lockout, and exports the local security policy before and after as proof of exactly what changed.

Second, disabling services that shouldn't be running. A clean Windows Server install starts more than a file server or work-order app actually needs. RemoteRegistry is a classic example -- legitimate uses elsewhere, but neither server needs it, so it gets disabled as unused attack surface.

Third, local administrator passwords. Both servers were sharing one password, set years ago and never rotated -- meaning one compromised credential was a compromised credential on both machines. Mara moves both to LAPS, which generates a unique, randomized password per server and rotates it automatically.

Fourth, Windows Firewall, scoped to the Domain profile only, since neither server ever legitimately sits on a Private or Public network -- inbound SMB is allowed only from Hartwell's management subnet, not from any address. Then gpresult slash r and a firewall filter check confirm every piece of this actually applied, not just got saved in a dialog box.
With the Windows side hardened and verified, next lesson does the same work on Hartwell's two Linux servers.
